references.text: Pharaoh's magicians (chartummim) are also mentioned here, as they attempt to mimic Moses' signs
Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said - the same wording is used
Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said - a repeated pattern
Pharaoh hardened his own heart again - part of the recurring motif of Pharaoh's hardening
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had told Moses
God predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart - the fulfillment of this promise
God's finger is mentioned in connection with His creative and mighty works
The tablets of the law were written by God's finger - the same expression for divine power
Jesus says that He casts out demons by the finger of God - an allusion to this event
Reference to the tablets written by God's finger - a parallel to the phrase 'finger of God'
Fingers of a human hand writing on the wall - divine intervention through finger symbolism
Both verses document Pharaoh's unyielding resistance, but 9:35 marks the end of a cycle where hardening has reached its ultimate goal.
The verses show the connection between Pharaoh's persistent resistance (8:15) and the final, active hardening that leads to the departure (14:8).
7:14 is the direct prophetic precursor to the event in 8:15, and together they show that Pharaoh's resistance was part of God's plan.
10:1 reveals the divine purpose behind the hardening observed in 8:15: that God's signs should become clear even to His opponents.
9:4 explains the theological purpose behind the hardening observed in 8:15: that God's glory may be revealed through Pharaoh's resistance.
